ledger.text: Chainguard unilaterally broke the embargo on 21 October at 07:41 UTC by publishing built images containing the fix
ledger.attributed_to: PHP Foundation; Chainguard's CEO accepts the time and denies leaking

factcheck.reason: The act and time (built images with the fix at 07:41 UTC on 21 October) are the Foundation's and Lorenc 'doesn't dispute the timeline' (The Register). 'Unilaterally broke the embargo' is the Foundation's reading; Lorenc says exploits were in the wild and he notified the coordinated disclosure channel first, which contests 'unilaterally'. Feross and The Hacker News restate the Foundation (one origin).
factcheck.next_step: Capture Chainguard's image publication record (registry timestamps) and Lorenc's own posts (LinkedIn, Hacker News); ask the PHP distros list for the notification message time.

ledger.attributed_to: social posts on 20 October, relayed by a vendor and a news site

factcheck.reason: The CVE records (the authoritative record for the score) give 9.2 under CVSS 4.0 for both flaws, and the PHP Foundation names 10.0 as a wrong score from the leak. The statement is refuted; the site's status 'contradicted' matches.

ledger.text: On 20 October at about 15:00 UTC the two CVE IDs began circulating on forums and social media with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS score; no technical details leaked

factcheck.reason: The Foundation states every element. The time and the CVE IDs circulating are corroborated independently (Equixly: Hacker News post 'about 15:20'; Huntress and CybelAngel: 'morning of October 20', which fits 15:00 UTC as US morning). 'No technical details leaked' is disputed: Daubois (PHP security team) describes a leaked tool screenshot and an exploitation video, and The Hacker News says a PoC leaked. The two Foundation slugs are the same page captured twice, not two sources.
factcheck.next_step: Capture the archived Hacker News post (the r/PHP thread links news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50176735 as context) and Florian Roth's CVSS 10.0 post.

ledger.text: Mitigation advice given to a few critical-infrastructure providers from about 23:00 UTC on 20 October may have leaked

factcheck.reason: The Foundation's own sentence carries every element, including its hedge 'may have leaked'. It is one party's self-report; The Register and SecurityWeek repeat it without new evidence.
factcheck.next_step: Ask the Foundation which providers and what evidence of the leak; look for the mitigation text circulating before release.

ledger.text: Calif mistakenly published a video around 20:00 UTC on 20 October showing its proof of concept against a number of targets; copies circulated and 'contributed to accelerated development of various PoCs'

factcheck.reason: The Foundation states it and the quoted phrase is verbatim; BBC, The Register, The Record and Feross echo the Foundation (one origin, A3). Daubois separately mentions a short exploitation video that went up and came down, without naming Calif. The time is uncertain: the Foundation's 'As a result of the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC' can attach '20:00 UTC' to the pre-announcement, which it puts at 19:30.
factcheck.next_step: Ask Calif for the time and content of the deleted video; capture any copy circulated on X.

ledger.text: OpenAI independently reported the same root cause on 11 August, with further vectors on 18 September

factcheck.reason: The Foundation's page says this word for word (one named primary party, the recipient of the reports). The GHSA credits and the CVE records corroborate that OpenAI was a credited reporter or finder but carry no dates. OpenAI's own account is blocked; Cybernews relays OpenAI as saying its researcher 'subsequently' found additional flaws after Calif, and the X Community Note disputes OpenAI's discovery role.
factcheck.next_step: Capture OpenAI's blog post; ask the PHP security team or OpenAI (Amy Burnett) for the GHSA report timestamps.

ledger.text: The pre-announcement was published at 19:30 UTC on 20 October

factcheck.reason: Only the PHP Foundation states 19:30 UTC, and the same post later says 'pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC'. The oss-security relay of the php.net text (Date 13:22:51 -0700 = 20:22:51Z) bounds it from above, and the feed's 20:32:00Z is later than that relay, so the feed time cannot be the publication time. One party's self-report, A2; 'disputed' fits.
factcheck.next_step: The php/web-php commit that added the 2026-10-20-1 archive entry, or the php-announce list message time.

ledger.text: The out-of-memory issue was found in a 2024 audit by Quarkslab (funded through OSTIF and the Sovereign Tech Agency) but exploitation was not proven, so it was not fixed

factcheck.reason: Calif says Quarkslab's audit 'rediscovered the same OOM issue' and 'exploitation was not proven, hence the bug was not fixed', but Calif says it confirmed this 'from PHP', so it is not independent of the Foundation. The Foundation says something different: a PHP core developer found the OOM signs while fixing a Quarkslab finding, and the fix stalled over trade-offs and resources, not only unproven exploitation. Quarkslab's own summary describes no OOM finding. Run 6: Cloudflare's post was edited on 23 October ('Today,' became 'October 21,'); Quarkslab is still named, so the grade stands.
factcheck.next_step: Ask Quarkslab or OSTIF whether any of the 27 findings (or redacted HIGH-1/MED-2) is the OOM issue; the full Quarkslab PDF report is linked from its blog and should be captured.

ledger.text: Remote code execution is confirmed on PHP-FPM
ledger.attributed_to: PHP Foundation blog; GHSA-6wmf for the session path

factcheck.reason: As worded, the claim is carried by the PHP security team's own advisory for CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf) and its oss-security post, which say RCE was demonstrated on a normal dynamic FPM pool, given a suitable application operation. What is disputed is which flaw does it: the Foundation's blog puts FPM under CVE-2026-109618, whose own advisory says no complete FPM exploit was shown (K-008). That does not touch this claim, so the site's 'disputed' understates it.
factcheck.next_step: A clarification from the PHP security team (oss-security reply or GHSA update) on whether CVE-2026-109618 has a demonstrated FPM exploit, or a correction of the Foundation blog, would settle the CVE attribution.

ledger.text: The release moved forward from 22 October 14:00 UTC to 21 October 14:00 UTC because of the leak
ledger.attributed_to: PHP Foundation; php.net pre-announcement; Wiz thread ('Apply the Oct 22 security release')

factcheck.reason: The new time (21 October 14:00 UTC) is in the php.net pre-announcement relayed to oss-security (record). That the original date was 22 October is carried by the Foundation and indirectly by Wiz's thread and the php.net ChangeLog; that the move was because of the leak, by the Foundation and Daubois. The original hour '14:00 UTC' rests on the Foundation alone (echoed by The Hacker News), while watchTowr (via Daubois, Huntress, CybelAngel) put the embargo at Thursday 11am ET, which is 15:00 UTC.
factcheck.next_step: Ask the PHP release managers or the distros list for the original embargo time; capture php/web-php commit history for the pre-announcement and release posts.

ledger.text: Calif found the flaws first: discovery 1 August, hash commitment 5 August, report to PHP 11 August

factcheck.reason: The dates under it are well carried: the hash tweet date is on X and the snowflake ID 2085031675382071483 decodes to 2026-08-05T15:54:24Z (A6); the 11 August report is in both Calif's and the Foundation's pages (A5); the 1 August discovery date is Calif's own word only (A2). 'Found the flaws first' is a reading (max A3): the Foundation says the OOM root cause was found in 2024, OpenAI reported the same root cause the same day, and nothing shows Calif found the second CVE first.
factcheck.next_step: Ask Calif (Ryan Austin) for the pre-image of d935be02...24ac; ask OpenAI (Amy Burnett, Codex Security) for its own discovery date.

ledger.text: Wiz Research independently discovered the first flaw on 19 August and reported on 24 August

factcheck.reason: Wiz's timeline carries 'discovers the first PHP vulnerability' on 19 August and the report on 24 August, and the Foundation independently confirms a Wiz report on 24 August. 'Independently' is not in any captured primary: Wiz itself says it worked with Calif and OpenAI 'on discovery', and the Foundation frames Wiz's report as 'further attack vectors'. 'The first flaw' means Wiz's first finding, not the first flaw overall.
factcheck.next_step: Ask Wiz whether it knew of Calif's or OpenAI's reports before 19 August; capture OpenAI's blog (says 'independently', per snippet).

timeline.what: Quarkslab audits PHP (funded through OSTIF and the Sovereign Tech Agency). While fixing one of its findings a PHP core developer finds the first signs of the out-of-memory problem behind CVE-2026-109618; an exploit is theorised but no vector found, so it is not fixed.
OpenAI launches Patch the Planet (a Daybreak initiative with Trail of Bits, HackerOne and Calif).
Calif begins an audit of PHP under Patch the Planet; Volker Dusch accepts the invitation.
Calif discovers 'multiple different paths independently leading to RCE that resurfaced the 2024 issues and new trigger points'.
Ryan Austin (@lcfr_hax) posts a SHA-256 hash on X as a commitment to one finding.
Calif reports the first bug to PHP and coordinated disclosure begins. OpenAI independently reports the same root cause the same day.
Calif shares an RCE proof of concept with PHP; PHP confirms it works on 15 August.
Wiz Research discovers the first vulnerability using Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol; confirms RCE against Drupal on 20 August and WordPress on 21 August.
Calif reports the second bug to PHP.
Wiz reports to the PHP security team.
The GitHub security advisory is opened, credited to lcfr-hax, sagitzadik-wiz, amyb-oai and tomash-areion.
Further attack vectors reported by OpenAI.
PHP acknowledges Wiz's reports 'and begins developing a coordinated fix'.
The fix pull request is opened.
Cloudflare starts developing WAF protections 'since early October 2026'.
CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are reserved.
An exploit attempt from an anonymisation-network IP hits an Amazon MadPot honeypot.
The final fix commit is authored; the 7.4 backport branch's commit is dated 18:10:24Z.
Arnaud Le Blanc authors the fix, 'Avoid state corruption via bailout', with Ilija Tovilo, Jakub Zelenka, Nora Dossche and Nicolas Grekas; the 7.4 minimal backport is authored at 18:09 UTC.
Release commits for 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 are made under embargo (14:00 to 17:04 UTC).
Qualys publishes on the pre-announcement.
Swiss BACS posts a warning (home-page teaser dated 20 October; the page itself now says 21 October).

The two CVE IDs begin circulating on forums and social media with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS of 10.0. Per Daubois: an anonymous Hacker News post, then screenshots, a 'PHP2Shell tool' screenshot credited to Calif.io, a short exploitation video, and watchTowr posting both CVE numbers.
php.net publishes the pre-announcement: release moved to 21 October 14:00 UTC, two critical vulnerabilities, CVSS v4.0 9.2, 'we reserve the right to release earlier'.
Calif 'mistakenly published a video' showing its proof of concept against several targets; copies circulate after it is deleted.
Alan Coopersmith relays the php.net pre-announcement to oss-security.
The PHP project starts giving mitigation advice to a few critical-infrastructure providers; it 'may have leaked as well'.

CISA alert 'Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching': take systems offline if you cannot update. NSA press release 'PHP2Shell'. UK NCSC alert. CCCS AL26-026. CERT-FR ALE-014. ACN AL07/261021. Cloudflare, Wiz, Calif, the PHP Foundation and Daubois publish their accounts.

The Dutch NCSC takes its own website offline as a precaution; DigiD, MijnOverheid and Overheid.nl follow. Weird Gloop turns off its wiki web servers for 13 hours. Amazon, Imperva, Fastly, Akamai and Huntress publish.
Amazon sees proof-of-concept attempts, then six hours of attempts from anonymised infrastructure.
Cloudflare's WAF protections go live for all customers, about nine hours ahead of disclosure.
Chainguard publishes built images containing the fix, 'more than six hours before the coordinated release'.
Cloudflare's CTO reports early attacks emerging, before the release.
ELLIO records its first sensor hit.
Finland's Valtori begins restricting public traffic to government web services (12:45 local).
CERT-EU's stated release time for the PHP fixes.
Wiz posts 'BREAKING ... #PHP2SHELL ... impacting 70% of the Internet', 28 minutes before the planned release; the thread still says 'Apply the Oct 22 security release'.
GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp (CVE-2026-109619) and, twelve seconds later, GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w (CVE-2026-109618) are published by bukka.
Signed tags php-8.5.12, php-8.4.27, php-8.3.36 and php-8.2.35 are created.
NSA Cybersecurity posts on X: 'Effective Immediately ... be prepared for an update addressing two critical vulnerabilities ... take the system offline'.
The CVE record for CVE-2026-109618 is published; CVE-2026-109619 follows at 13:54:43Z.
The planned release time. php.net's advisory 'Critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, update now' and the four release posts go up.
OpenAI posts: models 'helped researchers ... discover critical security flaws in PHP ... used to run an estimated 70% of websites'. An X Community Note later disputes OpenAI's role.
CISA releases KEV catalog version 2026.10.21; neither PHP CVE is in it.
The fix commit enters the public php-src branches (commit timestamp); merged into 8.3 at 14:12, 8.4 at 14:27 and 8.5 at 14:30 UTC.
GitHub release php-8.5.12 is published by adoy.
NVD publishes both CVEs with the CNA's CVSS v4.0 9.2 and no NIST score.
CISA's ADP assessment on both CVE records: exploitation none, automatable no, technical impact total.
Jakub Zelenka announces CVE-2026-109618 on oss-security; CVE-2026-109619 at 14:44:06Z.
CERT-EU Security Advisory 2026-018 (stated 15:20:18, timezone not given).
Aaron Rainbolt relays to oss-security a Fediverse report that the 8.5.12 fix may be incomplete; a Debian maintainer adds that the poster called it a different bug.
NCSC-NL's php2shell README last significant change (17:25 CEST). CERT.LV publishes: Latvia restricts access to several state digital resources from abroad (18:25 EEST).
Per a Matrix channel, Canonical asked PHP about the Fediverse report and was told it is 'unrelated and not a real issue'.
CERT.LV update: the unified state website platform is patched; lsm.lv and 112.lv restored; about 6,000 potentially affected resources in Latvia; automated attempts seen, none successful.
NCSC New Zealand: 'aware of reports of active exploitation' (09:15 NZDT 22 October; updated 21:20Z).
Huntress: no exploitation observed on partner systems (16:30 ET).
The Hacker News publishes Amazon's account of the 17 October honeypot attempt and VulnCheck's count of 2,608,039 hosts.
The Register carries Dan Lorenc's reply to the PHP Foundation; Fortinet publishes FortiWeb signatures; The Record carries the Foundation's account of the 2024 signs.
NSA Cybersecurity posts 'UPDATE: Specific mitigation guidance ... is now available', linking the press release.
Matthew Prince posts Cloudflare's attempt counts: thousands before, millions after.
JVN publishes its note (14:20 JST); JPCERT/CC alert JPCERT-AT-2026-0033 is dated 22 October.
BBC News opens its live page: 'Global scramble to fix critical cyber-security flaws as many websites taken offline'.
Greenbone on oss-security: the backports imply versions down to 7.4 are affected, whatever the subject line says.
The BBC reports the NSA's X post.
Ryan Austin on BBC Radio 4: no evidence of exploitation yet.
The UK NCSC page is modified (HTTP last-modified).
The evidence vault behind this site is opened; the first capture of the BBC live page is at 08:04:53Z.
NCSC-NL merges pull request 10; the inventory has 674 entries at commit cca173c64ec5.

CISA releases KEV catalog version 2026.10.26 (1,758 entries), adding CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: date added 26 October, due date 29 October for US federal civilian agencies, known ransomware use "Unknown". Its alert of the same day names no victim.

echo.from: notes and notes_md of sources.json, not the graph
echo.rule: case-insensitive, word-boundary match; the outlet's own sources excluded; claims = ledger claims the echo source also cites (graph-backed), not claims named in the notes

points.requests: outreach.json requests with actor == outlet actor, or whose said[].source is an outlet source, or whose publisher matches --publisher-match
points.proposed: carried by hand from the editor's briefing (editorial file), request_id null, not graded here; verdict is the fact-check verdict of the linked claim
points.their_words: the outlet's words as the fact-check desk quoted them from the capture (checked[] result carries/partial); null when the capture does not carry them
points.primary: the contradiction record's first statement not made by the outlet, else the first fact-check check on a non-outlet source, primary sources before secondary

method.timeline: lane outlet = timeline.json entries all of whose sources are the outlet's, plus the source published time when no such entry shares its minute; lane world = every other timeline.json entry (all 69 in the data; filter by t)
method.ledger: every claim in claims.json citing an outlet source, with factcheck.json assessment joined; by_verdict counts the fact-check verdict
limits: echo is read from free-text notes, not from graph edges; party:php-foundation has no incoming edge from the echo sources
the outlet's own entries (posts) are not in the data: only the source's published time and timeline.json entries that cite it; the raw __INITIAL_DATA__ posts are in the vault, not here
no capture is later than the newest in captures; the page cannot say what the outlet's page says now
capture content is never copied: stamps and file hashes only
